Email & Alerts settings

Configure how SATOM sends email (local relay or external SMTP) and the alert engine's delivery policy — which checks run, their limits, the cooldown, and which of the five sinks (bell, email, webhook, integration hooks, syslog/CEF) receive which findings.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereSettings → System → General → Email & Alerts (URL /settings/#tab-email)

What is it?#

The Email & Alerts tab holds two forms. Email (SMTP) Configuration is the mail transport every feature uses. Alerts & notifications is the delivery policy of the proactive health engine (satom-alerts.timer, every 15 minutes): which checks may raise findings, the limits they use, how often a finding may repeat, and where each finding is delivered. What counts as bad for probes and devices is measurement policy and lives on Thresholds.

What does it do?#

  • Sends mail through the node's local relay or an external SMTP server, with a Send test button.
  • Turns alert dispatch on or off and sets the alert recipients.
  • Enables or disables each of the eight checks: Cert expiry, Git divergence, Device health, Backup freshness, Config drift, Scheduled automation, Host resources, API catalog integrity.
  • Routes findings to five delivery sinks, each with its own on/off switch, minimum severity and family mask: In-app bell, Email, Webhook (HTTP POST), Integration hooks, Syslog / CEF feed.
  • Preview now (no send) evaluates every enabled check and shows what would fire.

The wire formats (webhook envelope and signature verification, RFC 5424/CEF field maps, the alert.fired payload) are documented in Alerting.

Requirements#

  • users.manage.
  • For external SMTP: host, port and (optionally) credentials of a mail server reachable from the node. For the webhook: an HTTP(S) endpoint. For syslog: a collector such as FortiAnalyzer or a SIEM.

Permissions#

🔑Permission

All routes (POST /settings/email, /settings/email/test, /settings/alerts, GET /settings/alerts/preview) require users.manage. Without it the System › General group is hidden and calls return 403.

How to use#

Configure email#

  1. Open Settings → System → General → Email & Alerts.
  2. Switch on Enable email sending, choose Server type, fill the fields and click Save email settings — "Email settings saved."
  3. In Send a test email, enter a Recipient and click Send test. The test uses the saved settings. Success shows e.g. "Sent to ops@example.com via smtp.example.com:587 (starttls)."

Configure alerts#

  1. In Alerts & notifications, switch on Enable alert dispatch, fill Alert recipient(s) and tick the Checks enabled.
  2. Adjust the limits on the right (see Configuration).
  3. In Delivery sinks, set each sink's On, Minimum severity and Families delivered.
  4. Fill Webhook endpoint and/or Syslog collector if you use those sinks.
  5. Click Save alert settings — "Alert settings saved."
  6. Click Preview now (no send). It lists the findings that would fire and the resolved recipients, e.g. "3 finding(s) would notify ops@example.com (nothing sent — preview only):" or "No findings — all checks green. Recipients: …"

Configuration#

Email (SMTP) Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Enable email sending Master switch for every outgoing email, default off. See the note below. No on
Server type Local mail server (localhost relay, no auth) (default) or External SMTP server (third-party). Local forces host localhost, no TLS, no authentication. Yes External
SMTP host External only. External smtp.example.com
Port Blank = default for the transport (25 / 587 / 465). No 587
Transport security None (plain, port 25) — insecure, STARTTLS (port 587), SSL / TLS (port 465). Default none. No STARTTLS
Verify TLS certificate Default on. Uncheck only for an internal server with a self-signed certificate (insecure). No on
Server requires authentication Default off. Turning it off forgets a stored password. No on
Username / Password Password stored encrypted; blank keeps the stored one. If auth satom@example.com
From name Default SATOM. No SATOM
From address Sender address. Email counts as configured only with a From address. Yes noreply@example.com
Default recipient(s) Comma / semicolon / newline separated; used when a notice has no explicit recipient. No ops@example.com
Timeout (seconds) 5–120, default 20. No 20

ℹ️Note — What "Enable email sending" stops

When it is off, SATOM sends no email at all: alert email, bug-report notifications, Certificate Manager notifications, change-request notifications, scheduled monitoring reports and password-reset links are all refused with Email sending is disabled (Settings → Email & Alerts). Only the Send test button still sends, so you can check the transport before switching it on. To silence only alert email, switch off the Email sink or Enable alert dispatch instead.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: switching Enable email sending off now stops every outgoing email; before, alert email, bug-report and Certificate Manager notifications were still sent.

Alerts & notifications#

Field Description Required Example
Enable alert dispatch Master switch, default off. Gates the Email, Webhook and Integration hooks sinks; the In-app bell and the Syslog feed ignore it. No on
Alert recipient(s) Blank falls back to the email Default recipient(s) (shown next to the field). No noc@example.com
Checks enabled Eight checks, all on by default. No all
Cert warn (days) 1–365, default 14. No 14
Cooldown (hours) Per-finding suppression window, 0–168, default 6. No 6
Git behind max Standby commits behind, 1–10000, default 25. No 25
Git unpushed max (hours) Age of a local commit that never reached the remote, 1–8760, default 6. No 6
Backup stale (hours) Newest system bundle older than this, 1–8760, default 48. No 48
Drift window (min) Only drift newer than this alerts, 1–43200, default 90. No 90
Change made through SATOM Report it, credited to its author (default), Report it as drift, credited to its author, Do not report it. Unexplained drift is always reported. No default
Automation fail streak → critical 2–100, default 3. No 3
Automation overdue (hours) 1–8760, default 3. No 3
Device alert floor Degraded and worse (default) or Critical only. No Critical only

Out-of-range numbers are clamped to the range on save.

Delivery sinks#

Sink Default Notes
In-app bell on, info, all families Always evaluated, independent of the master switch.
Email on, info, all families also needs the master switch above
Webhook (HTTP POST) off one POST per run, all-or-nothing — also needs the master switch
Integration hooks off one alert.fired per finding — enqueued, not delivered
Syslog / CEF feed off no cooldown — a record, not a recipient; emits from primary and standby

Per sink: Minimum severity info / warning / critical (unknown → info) and Families delivered (the eight check families). A sink with no family ticked shows the red badge delivers nothing. Engine failures and findings from unknown checks ignore both filters.

Webhook endpoint and Syslog collector#

Field Description Required Example
Endpoint URL Must start with http:// or https://; an invalid URL is stored and flagged in red. Private addresses are allowed. For webhook https://automation.example.com/hook/satom
Encoding (webhook) SATOM envelope (JSON) (default) or Slack-compatible ({"text": ...}) for Slack, Mattermost, Rocket.Chat. No SATOM
Timeout (s) 1–30, default 10. No 10
Retries 0–3, default 2; only 408, 425, 429 and 5xx are retried. No 2
Signing secret (HMAC-SHA256) Stored where the vault mode says (only in the vault at alerts/webhook in vault-only mode, otherwise encrypted in SATOM), never shown; blank keeps it. Badge set (plus in the vault) or not set — requests go unsigned. No —
Remove the stored secret Tick to delete the secret on save. No —
Collector host Syslog destination. For syslog faz.example.com
Port 1–65535, default 514. No 514
Transport UDP (default) or TCP. TLS is not implemented. No UDP
Encoding (syslog) RFC 5424 (default) or CEF. LEEF is not implemented. No CEF
Facility user, daemon, auth, syslog, authpriv, local0–local7; default local0. No local3

Example#

🧪Example — Critical alerts to chat, everything to the SIEM

  1. Webhook: URL of your chat bridge, Encoding Slack-compatible, sink On, minimum severity critical, all families.
  2. Syslog: collector siem.example.com, CEF, sink On, minimum severity info.
  3. Email: sink On, families Cert expiry and Backup freshness only.
  4. Enable alert dispatch on, save, then Preview now (no send).

Result#

  • Settings are stored in app_settings (email.*, alerts.*, alerts.sink.*, alerts.webhook.*, alerts.syslog.*); audit entries settings.email, settings.email_test and settings.alerts.
  • On the next engine run (every 15 minutes) findings are routed per sink. The six limits shared with the SATOM (the application) scope on Thresholds are the same stored values.

Troubleshooting#

"Enter a recipient (or set a default recipient)."#

Solution — type a Recipient in the test card or set Default recipient(s) and save.

"No 'From' address configured."#

Solution — fill From address (or a username) and save before testing.

"Authentication failed: …"#

Possible causes — wrong username or password, or the server needs an app password.

Solution — re-enter the password (blank keeps the old one), save, test again.

"SSLError: …" or "ConnectionRefusedError: …"#

Possible causes — the transport security does not match the port, the certificate is not trusted, or a firewall blocks the port.

Solution — use STARTTLS on 587 or SSL/TLS on 465; for an internal CA either trust it on the node or (insecurely) untick Verify TLS certificate.

A device is red but no mail arrived#

Possible causes - Enable alert dispatch is off, or the Email sink is off, masked, or its severity floor is above the finding. - Device alert floor is Critical only and the device is only degraded. - The finding fired within the Cooldown window.

Solution — click Preview now (no send); it shows what would fire and the resolved recipients.

The webhook URL shows "URL must start with http:// or https://" or "URL has no host"#

Solution — correct the Endpoint URL and save; the value is kept and flagged until fixed.

Advanced#

Advanced Behaviour worth knowing
  • The bell, email, webhook and hook sinks share the cooldown; the syslog feed has none and is not counted as dispatched. Hooks are counted as queued, never dispatched.
  • A finding no notification sink accepted is not stamped for cooldown, so widening a filter later delivers it on the next run.
  • Mail subjects read [SATOM/<node>] N alert(s) — <first title>.
  • The preview endpoint also returns per-sink counts (routed) as JSON; the page itself shows the findings and recipients only.
